public_rationale: Early TruthfulQA results support Marcus's concern: larger models in the tested families were generally less truthful. But research available before his post also found that larger Gopher models performed better on TruthfulQA's multiple-choice task, including evaluation variants. Thus the no-improvement pattern held in some settings and failed in others. The evidence supports a narrower, model-dependent claim, not the broad statement as written. The separate claim that scaling increased apparent authority remains unestablished by a direct measure.
limitations: The supporting and opposing studies use different model families and partly different evaluation formats.
Multiple-choice accuracy measures recognition of truthful answers, not directly the truthfulness of generated writing.
The authority component remains unsettled; mixed does not mean both halves were fully measured.
No post-February 2023 model improvements are used to judge the historical claim.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Scaling neural network models has made their output more authoritative-sounding but not more truthful.

statement.excerpt: Scaling neural network models—making them bigger—has made their faux writing more and more authoritative-sounding, but not more and more truthful.
statement.document_title: Oops! How Google bombed, while doing pretty much exactly the same thing as Microsoft did, with similar results

from_speaker: Scaling neural network models—making them bigger
our_interpretation: This describes effects observed by February 9, 2023, rather than forecasting the effects of future scaling. No beginning date is supplied.
The context concerns language models generating text, rather than every kind of neural network.
The ordinary reading is that increasing model size had improved apparent authority without a corresponding improvement in factual truthfulness.
Truthfulness means giving factually correct answers. Authoritative-sounding means appearing confident or convincing; fluency or resemblance to human writing is only indirect evidence.
Within-family comparisons across parameter counts are the most relevant tests. Improvements caused solely by different training objectives or prompting do not establish a size effect.

A mixed outcome is appropriate if the no-improvement pattern holds for some tested model families but other comparable tests show gains. An unmeasured authority component remains explicitly unsettled.
criteria.support_condition: Controlled size comparisons show increasingly authoritative output without increasing factual truthfulness. Evidence limited to particular model families supports only that part of the generalization.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable size-controlled evaluations show factual truthfulness improving with model size, or direct evaluations show that apparent authority does not increase.
